THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, APRIL 16, 1937

FEARED DEPORTATION
Soviet Law

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—In reply to INTERESTED, whose letter appeared in your paper on the 13th inst., under the heading: "Feared Deportation" "White Russian's Arrest," I wish to state the following:

In the Soviet Criminal Code there is (or at least there was in 1927 when I for the last time saw that code) an article stating that anyone having left U.S.S.R. without special permission is to be exiled from that country forever. In case of his returning to the U.S.S.R. he is to be subjected to his "supreme penalty," which terms is used by the Code instead of saying "Is to be shot." It is further stated in the article, if I remember correctly, that a special permission to return may be granted by the authorities of the U.S.S.R. In such case the returning man may be exempted from that "supreme penalty."

I happen to know a case of a White Russian who had applied for and received that special permission to return. Soon after he was arrested by the G.P.U. and after a few months in the gaol was executed. He was not even given the fairness of an open trial in the court, but his case was simply dealt with by the Collegium of the G.P.U.—as is mostly done with political offenders.

If Vladimir Moskvitin would be deported to the U.S.S.R. it could be done only after the authorities of that country would agree to admit him, but they would agree only with the same intention as it was in the case of the White Russian who was executed. In the case of Moskvitin the matter is still more aggravated by the fact that his trying to deface the emblem on the doors of the Soviet Consulate is undoubtedly a very grave political offence against the country to which he would be deported, and the result for him would be death, even if the article referred to above has been in the meantime cancelled.

In ordering the deportation of Moskvitin, the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court was evidently influenced by the fact that Moskvitin had committed the same offence twice, and that he is the third man trying to deface the Soviet emblem. Were it possible to deport Moskvitin to any country other than U.S.S.R., everything "would be in order," using the expression of INTERESTED, but Moskvitin does not belong to any country, and it is very likely that no country will accept him. In that case it is the duty of Russian organisations of Shanghai to respectfully draw the attention of the authorities concerned to the fact that deportation of Moskvitin to U.S.S.R. would be equivalent to indirectly inflicting death for an offence for which, according to Art. 118, Chapter III of the Criminal Code of the Republic of China, the highest penalty is one year of imprisonment.

I am not entitled to speak on behalf of any of the Russian organizations, but I hope they will not shirk their responsibility. As to myself, I am prepared to appear in the court as a witness, if necessary, and after being duly sworn, to state to the Court the reasons of my belief that deportation to the U.S.S.R. would be equivalent for Moskvitin to a death verdict. Russian organisations competent to handle this case are being simultaneously advised of my preparedness to assist them.

Witness.
Shanghai, Apr. 15.

《字林西报》，1937年4月16日，星期五

担忧被驱逐出境
苏联法律

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——回复“INTERESTED”（热心读者）于本月13日贵报刊登的题为“担忧被驱逐出境”、“白俄被捕”的来信，本人谨陈述如下：

在《苏维埃刑法典》中有一条款规定（或者至少在我最后一次看到该法典的1927年是如此），任何未经特别许可离开苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（U.S.S.R.）的人，将被永远流放出国。如果此人返回苏联，他将受到“最高刑罚”，法典使用这一术语来代替“处决”。如果我记得没错的话，该条款还规定，苏联当局可以授予返回的特别许可。在这种情况下，返回者可以免除那种“最高刑罚”。

我碰巧知道一个白俄案例，他申请并获得了这种返回的特别许可。但他回来后不久就被国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）逮捕，在监狱里关了几个月后被处决。他甚至没有得到法院公开审判的公正待遇，他的案件 simply 由国家政治保卫局委员会处理——这通常是处理政治犯的方式。

如果弗拉基米尔·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Moskvitin）被驱逐到苏联，那只能在该国当局同意接收他之后进行，但他们同意的意图将与上述被处决的白俄案例相同。在莫斯克维京一案中，情况更加严重，因为他试图污损苏联领事馆门上的徽章，这无疑是对他将要被驱逐到的国家犯下的非常严重的政治罪行，即使上述条款在此期间已被取消，其结果对他来说也是死亡。

江苏高等法院第二分院在命令驱逐莫斯克维京时，显然受到了以下事实的影响：莫斯克维京两次犯下同样的罪行，而且他是第三个试图污损苏联徽章的人。如果可以将莫斯克维京驱逐到苏联以外的任何国家，用“INTERESTED”的话说，一切都会“井然有序”，但莫斯克维京不属于任何国家，很可能没有国家会接受他。在这种情况下，上海的俄罗斯组织有责任恭敬地提请有关当局注意，将莫斯克维京驱逐到苏联相当于间接地对一项根据《中华民国刑法》第三章第118条最高刑罚仅为一年监禁的罪行判处死刑。

我无权代表任何俄罗斯组织发言，但我希望他们不会推卸责任。至于我自己，如有必要，我准备出庭作证，并在正式宣誓后，向法庭陈述我认为驱逐到苏联对莫斯克维京而言等同于死刑判决的理由。同时已通知有能力处理此案的俄罗斯组织，我准备协助他们。

证人。
上海，4月15日。

归档
J.B.R.
7/4

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 7, 1937

WHITE RUSSIAN TO
BE DEPORTED

Young Man Who Defaced
Soviet Emblem

For the first time since the treaty
between China and the U.S.S.R. was
signed, a Russian emigrant in Shang-
hai is to be deported, as a result of
a judgment delivered by the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court.
Vladimir Moskeitin, 24-year old White
Russian artist, was sentenced by the
Court to eight months' imprisonment,
followed by deportation. Court offi-
cials when interviewed yesterday
were unable to state where he would
be deported to, but indications are
that Moskeitin will be sent either to
Harbin or to the U.S.S.R.
According to the prosecution, at the
beginning of the year Moskeitin was
living alone in Wayside, and while
passing the Soviet Consulate on his
way to the French Concession one
day, he damaged the emblem on the
door. He was arrested, and detained
at the Hongkew Police Station.
Judgment was given in his case
yesterday, sentence being passed in
accordance with Article 118 of the
Penal Code of the Republic of China.
Enquiries at the Soviet Consulate
yesterday revealed that although a
number of White Russians were de-
ported to Vladivostock for various
offences prior to 1933, none have been
deported since the signing of the
treaty between China and Soviet
Russia.

《字林西报》，1937年4月7日，星期三

白俄将被驱逐出境

污损苏联徽章的青年

自中国与苏联签订条约以来，一名在上海的俄罗斯移民首次将被驱逐出境，这是江苏高等法院第二分院作出判决的结果。24岁的白俄艺术家弗拉基米尔·莫斯凯廷（Vladimir Moskeitin）被法院判处八个月监禁，随后驱逐出境。法院官员昨日在接受采访时无法说明他将被驱逐到哪里，但有迹象表明莫斯凯廷将被送往哈尔滨或苏联。

据检方称，今年年初，莫斯凯廷独自居住在韦赛德（Wayside，音译），有一天在前往法租界的途中经过苏联领事馆时，他损坏了门上的徽章。他被捕并被拘留在虹口警察局。

他的案件于昨日宣判，判决依据是《中华民国刑法》第118条。

昨日向苏联领事馆查询获悉，虽然在1933年之前有许多白俄人因各种罪行被驱逐到符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），但自中国与苏俄签订条约以来，没有人被驱逐出境。

（批注：d.S.C. - wu + yan bdy.
DBR 94.）

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 18, 1936

Russian Tells Reason For
Throwing Rocks At Consulate

Vladimir Moskvitin, Russian, told the 2nd Kiangsu High Court yesterday morning the reason he threw a stone at the Soviet Consulate-General early on the morning of June 9. The man is being tried under Article 118 of the Chinese Criminal Code on a charge of insulting a friendly foreign power and causing malicious damage.

He explained that he happened to be passing the consulate on Whangpoo Road and that just looking at the building reminded him of what he claimed to be his sufferings at the hands of the Soviets.

The more he thought about the days of the revolution in Russia, he declared, the more tempted he became to throw something at the Consulate. Finally, he picked up a stone and hurled it at the consulate door. The stone hit the U.S.S.R. emblem above the door.

He declared that he didn't mean to hit the emblem. He aimed at the door, he said, but the stone went wild. He also was alleged to have thrown some mud at the emblem but this he denied. He admitted that it was raining at the time but added that he threw no mud.

He was shown pictures taken of the emblem after the incident and they showed two or three splotches of mud. At this, the accused man declared that if mud had been thrown, it must have been someone else who did the throwing. The case was remanded on week for judgment.

《大美晚报》，1936年7月18日，星期六

俄罗斯人讲述向领事馆
扔石头的理由

俄罗斯人弗拉基米尔·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Moskvitin）昨日上午向江苏高等法院第二分院讲述了他在6月9日凌晨向苏联总领事馆扔石头的原因。该男子正根据《中华民国刑法》第118条受审，罪名是侮辱友好外国强国及造成恶意破坏。

他解释说，他碰巧路过黄浦路（Whangpoo Road）的领事馆，仅仅看着那座建筑就让他想起了他声称在苏联人手中遭受的苦难。

他说，他越是回想俄国革命的日子，就越忍不住想向领事馆扔东西。最后，他捡起一块石头扔向领事馆的大门。石头击中了门上方的苏联徽章。

他声称他无意击中徽章。他说他瞄准的是门，但石头扔偏了。还有人指控他向徽章扔了一些泥巴，但他予以否认。他承认当时正在下雨，但补充说他并没有扔泥巴。

向他展示了事件发生后拍摄的徽章照片，照片显示有两三处泥斑。对此，被告声称如果有人扔了泥巴，那一定是别人扔的。案件延期一周宣判。

法官问被告：-

问：1936年6月9日凌晨12点15分，你是否向黄浦路（Hangpoo Road，原文拼写错误，应为Whangpoo）20号的苏联领事馆辖区扔了石头？

答：是的。

问：这就是你使用的那块石头吗？

答：是的。

问：苏联国徽有任何损坏吗？

答：没有。我甚至连玻璃板都没打破。

问：你是“白俄”吗？

答：是的。

问：你憎恨并反对苏联政府吗？

答：我不喜欢它。它使我陷入贫困。

问：你有意打破徽章吗？

答：没有。当时正在下雨。我独自走在路上 **〔此处转录不清〕**，不知道如何获取食物和衣物来维持生计。想到我所有的痛苦都是苏联政府造成的，我捡起石头，没有任何特定目标地扔向建筑物。我相信它甚至根本没有碰到建筑物。

问：以前发生过类似的犯罪行为。罪犯是你的同伙吗？

答：不是。

问：你以前被判过刑吗？

答：没有。

问：你在上海有亲戚吗？

Barton:- At 12.15a.m. on the 9th. inst., I was on patrol duty on Whangpoo Rd near the Garden Bridge, when a ricksha coolie came and informed me that an unknown foreigner had thrown a stone at the building of the U.S.S.R. Consulate. I went there and picked up the stone on the door step. I also found some mud on the door. I then went around the vicinity and saw the accused standing on the road. On being questioned, he could not give me a satisfactory answer. I therefore arrested and brought him to the Station. On the way he confessed to having thrown the stone.

Q. What was accused's object, to break the door or the emblem?
A. Presumably, he threw it at the emblem, which was also spoiled with mud.

(F.P.S's Barton's evidence was interpreted to the accused).

Judge to accused:-
Q. The policeman stated that the emblem was spoiled with mud?
A. This is incorrect. Even so is it, how it can be proved that I had thrown the stone at it. It is quite possible that some other persons had spoiled it. Your Honour can see that the stone does not bear much mud.

Mr. Kumi:- The door of the U.S.S.R. Consulate is comparatively larger, and the glass occupies one third of it. MOSKVITIN CHARGED WITH
INSULTING FOREIGN STATE

An additional charge of offering
insult to a friendly foreign state was
specified in the Settlement Chinese
court yesterday against Vladimir
Moskvitin, a White Russian, who was
arrested on June 9 by Hongkew police
on the charge of attempting to cause
malicious damage to the local U.S.S.R.
Consulate-General, 20 Whangpoo
Road, by throwing a stone at the
premises. The additional charge was
preferred on the ground that the
prisoner did soil with mud the
national emblem affixed to the door
of the Soviet embassy. The First
District Court ruled that, insofar as
the additional charge was concerned,
only the Second High Court was com-
petent to hear the case, so it ordered
the accused to be transferred to the
said High Court for trial. The High
Court then ordered the accused to be
detained, pending the production of
the files. The accused had admitted
having thrown a stone at the local
Soviet Consulate-General, as he was
dissatisfied with the Soviet Govern-
ment.

莫斯克维京被控
侮辱外国国家

昨日，在上海特区法院对白俄弗拉基米尔·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Moskvitin）增加了一项指控，即侮辱友好外国国家。莫斯克维京于6月9日被虹口警方逮捕，罪名是企图通过向位于黄浦路20号的苏联驻沪总领事馆投掷石块，恶意损坏该馆舍。提出此项附加指控的理由是，囚犯用泥土污损了贴在苏维埃大使馆门上的国徽。第一特区法院裁定，就附加指控而言，只有江苏高等法院第二分院有权审理此案，因此命令将被告移送至该高等法院受审。高等法院随后命令羁押被告，待卷宗提交后处理。被告承认曾向当地苏联总领事馆投掷石块，因为他对苏维埃政府感到不满。

Russian Youth To
Face Charges Of
Stoning Consulate

Vladimir Maskovitch, age 22
Russian, who threw three stones
at the Soviet Consulate-General
shortly after the noon hour on
June 6, was handed over yester-
day morning by the First Special
District Court to the 2nd Kiangsu
High Court where he must stand
trial on insulting a friendly
foreign power. The man was
charged in the lower court with
causing malicious damage by
throwing both mud and stones at
the consulate.
Maskovitch declared yesterday
that he had thrown no mud at
the Soviet Consulate but ad-
mitting throwing stones at the
building. He would give no reason
for his action and the case was
adjourned for another week.

俄国青年将面临
砸击领事馆的指控

22岁的俄国人弗拉基米尔·马斯科维奇（Vladimir Maskovitch）于6月6日中午过后不久向苏联总领事馆投掷了三块石头，昨日上午由第一特区地方法院移交给江苏高等法院第二分院，他必须在那里接受关于侮辱友好邦交国的审判。该男子在下级法院被控通过向领事馆投掷泥土和石块造成恶意损害。

Subject V.P. Moskvitin, Russian arrested for attacking the local Soviet

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by L. J. J. [签名]

Vladimir Petrovitch Moskvitin is a Russian who was born
on May 27, 1914, at Blagoveschensk, Amur Province, Siberia.
He left Russia for Manchuria in 1922 together with his parents
and resided in Harbin where he attended a local primary school.
His father, who prior to the revolution in Russia was a Chief
Forester in the Amur Cossacks region, disappeared from Harbin
after a few years' residence in that city, and it is believed
that he committed suicide.

Upon leaving the school Moskvitin was employed in a haber-
dashery store for some time and in 1927 attended a ballet-
school in Harbin for four months, after which he became a
professional ballet dancer. He worked in this capacity in
various cabarets in Harbin for several months, after which he
was unemployed and resided with his mother who at that time was
the common law wife of one I.I. Travnikoff, ex-officer, and
an employee of the Harbin Police.

Towards the end of 1928 Moskvitin joined Bulatoff's Ballet
Company with which he visited Mukden, Tientsin and Peiping.

On August 5, 1931 he arrived in Shanghai. Here he worked
in his professional capacity in various cabarets and later also
visited Dairen, Hangchow, Hankow, Wusieh, Nanking and Soochow.
For the past several months he worked at the St. Georges Continent-
al Cabaret, Ningpo Road, and from May 4 to May 6 at the Cafe de
Paris, Rue Brenier de Montmorand, after which he has been
unemployed.

（批：FILE ...）

He keeps some of his belongings at Apt. 13, No. 505 Route
Vallon, a boarding-house owned by Mrs. Streltsova, where he
resided from March 15 until June 1, after which he has been
without a fixed abode. He still owes $12. to Mrs. Streltsova

主题 V.P. 莫斯克维京，俄国人，因袭击当地苏联领事馆被捕。

撰写人 D.S. Tcheremshansky 呈送人 L. J. J. [签名]

弗拉基米尔·彼得罗维奇·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Petrovitch Moskvitin）是一名俄国人，1914年5月27日出生于西伯利亚阿穆尔省布拉戈维申斯克。1922年，他与父母一起离开俄罗斯前往满洲，居住在哈尔滨，并在当地一所小学就读。他的父亲在俄国革命前曾是阿穆尔哥萨克地区的首席林业官，在哈尔滨居住几年后失踪，据信是自杀身亡。

离校后，莫斯克维京曾在一家服饰用品店工作了一段时间，1927年在哈尔滨的一所芭蕾舞学校学习了四个月，之后成为职业芭蕾舞者。他在哈尔滨的各种歌舞厅以这一身份工作了几个月，随后失业，与母亲同住。当时他的母亲是前军官、哈尔滨警察局雇员I.I. Travnikoff的事实婚姻妻子。

1928年底，莫斯克维京加入了布拉托夫（Bulatoff）芭蕾舞团，随团访问了沈阳、天津和北平。

1931年8月5日，他抵达上海。在此，他以职业身份在各种歌舞厅工作，后来还去过大连、杭州、汉口、无锡、南京和苏州。过去几个月，他在宁波路的圣乔治大陆歌舞厅（St. Georges Continental Cabaret）工作，5月4日至5月6日在蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）的巴黎咖啡馆（Cafe de Paris）工作，此后一直失业。

（批注：FILE ...）

他将部分物品存放在华伦路505号13室公寓，这是一处由斯特列尔佐娃（Streltsova）夫人拥有的寄宿公寓，他从3月15日居住至6月1日，此后居无定所。他仍欠斯特列尔佐娃夫人12美元

    Moskvitin was a member of the 3rd (Volunteer) Company of
the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., from 28.11.32 till 12.6.36, when
he was dismissed in connection with his arrest. He stated
that for a few months in 1932 he was a member of the "Union
of Monarchist Youth" in Shanghai (the organization does not
exist at present) and that since that time he did not belong
to any political group. He also stated that he was not
instigated by any persons to commit the offence but that he
did it under a sudden impulse, when, being without a fixed
abode and feeling miserable, he saw the Soviet Consulate and
thought that the Soviet regime **〔此处转录不清〕** to blame for his sufferings.
It is reported that Moskvitin is inclined to dissipated,
Bohemian mode of living. Although he is known as an anti-
Bolshevik, he does not seem to be interested in politics very
much.
    Moskvitin has three brothers, one of whom resides in
Harbin together with his mother, and one is employed as a
railway guard at Huhai Railway, Manchoukuo. The third brother,
Nicolay P. Moskvitin, is in Shanghai and is employed as a watch-
man at the Broadway Mansions.

(k) Are they all "old" servants?
(l) If not, what was their last employment
and for how long?
(m) What was their "characters"?
(n) If any suspicion attached to any of
them and if so, which one and for what
reason?
(o) Are old servants suspected?
(p) Are friends and visitors above suspicion
if not, who is suspected?

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 12.50 am, 9/6/36, F.P.S. 157 Barton brought
to the station the accused described on Sheet 1, whom
he had arrested on the Garden Bridge, he (P.S.Barton)
having been informed by a person in the vicinity that
the accused had thrown a stone at the windows of the
U.S.S.R. Consulate, No. 20 Whangpoo Road.

The accused, questioned by the undersigned and
F.S. Federoff, admitted that at about 12.15 am,
9/6/36, he had passed the U.S.S.R. Consulate, and
that out of hatred to U.S.S.R. Officials, he had then
thrown a small stone at the Consulate windows.

He had picked the stone up from the roadway on
N.Szechuen Rd. a few minutes previously.

A visit was paid to the scene, and it found that
the stone thrown by the accused had passed through
the iron framework of the Soviet emblem, and had hit
the window behind same, there being the mark of mud,
with which the stone was covered, on the window.

The stone throw by the accused was found under-
neath the window by P.S.Barton, the window itself,
however, being undamaged.

The accused denies having been instigated to
commit the offence by any other person, and states
that he does not belong to any political party.

Owing to the late hour, no person inside the
U.S.S.R. Consulate could be located.

The accused has been charged under Art. 388 (3)
of the CCRC, appearing before the S.S.D.Court on the
9/6/36, when a remand will be requested, to enable
further enquiries to be made.

J.R.
9/6

Whoumpson

备注
（任何突出或特殊的特征需由调查警官评论）。

1936年6月9日凌晨12:50，巡捕157号巴顿（F.P.S. 157 Barton）将在第1页描述的被告带到警局，他是在外白渡桥逮捕该被告的。巴顿巡捕（P.S.Barton）是从附近某人处得知被告向黄浦路20号苏联领事馆的窗户投掷了石块。

被告经下述签署人和联邦警探（F.S. Federoff）讯问后承认，1936年6月9日凌晨12:15左右，他经过苏联领事馆，出于对苏联官员的仇恨，他当时向领事馆窗户投掷了一块小石头。

几分钟前，他从北四川路的马路上捡起了这块石头。

经前往现场查看，发现被告投掷的石头穿过了苏联徽章的铁框架，击中了后面的窗户，窗户上有石头所带泥污的痕迹。

巴顿巡捕（P.S.Barton）在窗户下方发现了被告投掷的石头，然而窗户本身并未受损。

被告否认受任何人唆使犯罪，并声明他不属于任何政党。

由于时间已晚，未能找到苏联领事馆内的任何人员。

被告依据《中华民国刑法》第388条第3款被起诉，将于1936年6月9日出庭上海特区地方法院，届时将申请延期审理，以便进行进一步调查。

J.R.

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 10, 1936

Russian Youth Admits
Stoning Consulate

Because he threw a stone at the
Soviet Consulate-General shortly
after midnight yesterday, Vladimir
Moskvitin, age 22, Russian, was
brought before the First Special
District Court yesterday morning
and charged with maliciously
causing damage to the consulate.
The man admitted in court that
he had thrown the stone and would
have thrown another had he not
been apprehended by a constable.
He was trying to break a window,
he declared, and having missed with
his first shot, was all ready to try
again. The case was remanded until
June 16.

82.

《字林西报》，1936年6月10日，星期三

俄国青年承认向领事馆投掷石块

弗拉基米尔·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Moskvitin），22岁，俄国人，因于昨日午夜过后不久向苏联总领事馆投掷石块，于昨日上午被提解至第一特区地方法院受审，被控恶意损坏领事馆财产。该男子在法庭上承认曾投掷石块，并称若非被一名巡捕 apprehended（逮捕），他本会再投一块。他声称自己试图打破一扇窗户，第一击未中后，已准备好再次尝试。本案延期至6月16日审理。

82.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 10, 1936

STONE THROWN AT SOVIET
CONSULATE-GENERAL

Accused of attempting to cause
malicious damage to the premises of
the local Soviet Consulate-General, 20
Whangpoo Road, Vladimir Moskvitin,
aged 22, was arraigned before the
First Special District Court yesterday
and remanded for one week. The
accused, at 12.30 a.m. yesterday,
hurled a stone at the Consulate
window. F. S. 157 in the vicinity of
the Garden Bridge was informed and
he found the stone below the door
step, but the window was not broken.
The accused admitted the offence and
said he intended to damage the
Soviet emblem because he was not
satisfied with the Soviet Government.

《北华捷报》，1936年6月10日，星期三

有人向苏联总领事馆投掷石块

弗拉基米尔·莫斯克维京（Vladimir Moskvitin），22岁，被控企图恶意损坏位于黄浦路20号的本地苏联总领事馆处所，昨日于第一特区地方法院出庭受审，并还押候审一周。据称，被告于昨日凌晨12时30分向领事馆窗户投掷石块。外班巡捕第157号（F. S. 157）接到外白渡桥附近的通知后赶赴现场，他在门阶下方发现了石块，但窗户并未破碎。被告承认该项罪行，并表示其意图损毁苏联徽记，因为他对苏联政府感到不满。
